# Copilot Instructions — 2D Platformer (Godot 4.6)

## Project Overview

A 2D side-scrolling platformer built in **Godot 4.6** (GL Compatibility renderer).
Resolution: **640×360**, stretch mode `canvas_items`, run/main scene `res://scenes/level_1.scn`.
The game is a Deymoon character template designed so students can swap in their own Piskel sprite exports
without touching any code.

---

## Architecture

### Scripts

| File | Node type | Purpose |
|------|-----------|---------|
| `scripts/player.gd` | `CharacterBody2D` | Full player state machine (13 states) |
| `scripts/enemy.gd` | `CharacterBody2D` | Patrol + proximity-chase AI |
| `scripts/enemy_generator.gd` | `Node2D` | Proximity-triggered enemy spawner |
| `scripts/exit_zone.gd` | `Area2D` | Advances to next numbered level |
| `scripts/main.gd` | `Node2D` | HUD wiring (minimal) |

### Scenes

| Scene | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| `scenes/player.tscn` | Text scene; inline `AtlasTexture` sub-resources, one per animation frame |
| `scenes/enemy.tscn` | Reuses player sprites with an invert color `ShaderMaterial` |
| `scenes/enemy_generator.tscn` | Contains `SpawnTimer`, `SpawnPoint` (Marker2D), `TriggerArea` (CircleShape2D) |
| `scenes/exit_zone.tscn` | Area2D; auto-detects next level by filename number |
| `scenes/level_1.scn` … `level_6.scn` | **Binary `.scn` format** — do not open/edit as plain text |

### Addon

`addons/godot_mcp/` — an **editor-only** WebSocket MCP server for Claude AI integration.
Never import or call its APIs from game scripts.

---

## Player State Machine

States are plain **strings** (not enums). Exact spellings matter:

```
idle, walk, run, roll, jump, air_spin, land,
crouch_idle, crouch_walk,
ledge_grab, ledge_climb,
wall_slide, wall_land
```

Transitions flow through `_go(state: String)` which updates `self.state`, calls `_play()`,
and nudges `sprite.position` for ledge states.
`_play()` falls back to `"idle"` with `push_warning()` if the animation is missing — it will
**not** crash, by design (student-friendly).

### Key physics constants

```gdscript
WALK_SPEED  = 120.0    RUN_SPEED  = 220.0
JUMP_FORCE  = -420.0   GRAVITY    = 980.0
ROLL_SPEED  = 300.0    ROLL_TIME  = 0.4
WALL_GRAV   = 120.0    WALL_MAX   = 50.0
```

### Double-jump tracking

`jumps` counts jumps in the current airborne sequence: 0 → 1 on first jump, 1 → 2 on double-jump.
Walking off a ledge (floor→air transition while in `"jump"` state) sets `jumps = 1` to allow
exactly one air jump.

### Sprite position offsets per state

```gdscript
"ledge_grab"   → Vector2( 0, -10)
"ledge_climb"  → Vector2(18, -38)
default        → Vector2( 0, -16)
```
Do not change these without auditing every state transition.

### Dual use of the "roll" input action

- `Input.is_action_just_pressed("roll")` on floor + moving → initiates roll
- `Input.is_action_pressed("roll")` → enables run mode (hold Shift to run)

---

## Enemy

- Finds the player via `get_tree().get_first_node_in_group("player")` — **player must be in the `"player"` group**.
- Uses `RayLeft` and `RayRight` (`RayCast2D` children) for ledge detection during patrol.
- Uses `is_on_wall_only()` (not `is_on_wall()`) to avoid false-positives at floor edges.
- Renders with an invert color shader defined inline in `enemy.tscn`.

---

## Enemy Generator

- `@export` vars: `spawn_time_min`, `spawn_time_max`, `max_enemies`, `activation_radius`
- `TriggerArea` has `collision_layer = 0`, `collision_mask = 1` — player must be on **physics layer 1**.
- Uses `is_instance_valid(e)` to filter freed enemies from `_alive_enemies`; always use this
  instead of `!= null` for Godot objects.

---

## Exit Zone

Level filenames **must end with a number** (e.g. `level_3.tscn`). The script uses `RegEx` to
extract the trailing number, increments it, and scans the same directory for a matching file.
Supports both `.tscn` and `.scn` extensions.

Scene changes are deferred with `call_deferred("_go_to_next_level")` to avoid modifying the
scene tree inside a physics callback — keep this pattern when adding similar transitions.

---

## Godot 4-Specific Gotchas

### Resource UIDs
Every `.gd` file has a companion `.gd.uid` sidecar. **Never manually edit `.uid` files.**
Godot regenerates them; editing breaks resource references silently.

### Binary vs text scenes
Levels 1–6 use the **binary `.scn` format**. Do not attempt to parse or generate them as text.
New scenes created from scratch should use `.tscn` (text) for readability and version control.

### `.png.import` files
Auto-generated by Godot on first import. **Do not hand-edit them.** Deleting one forces a
reimport on next editor open. All player sprites in `sprites/player/` are 48×48 px per frame,
single-row spritesheets.

### AnimatedSprite2D frame layout
Frames are `AtlasTexture` sub-resources embedded directly in `player.tscn`. Adding a new
animation requires adding the correct number of `AtlasTexture` sub-resources with the right
`Rect2` regions, then wiring them into the `SpriteFrames` resource — the Godot editor UI is
the safest way to do this.

### `is_on_floor()` timing
In Godot 4, `is_on_floor()` returns the result from the **previous frame's** `move_and_slide()`.
The `prev_on_floor` variable in `player.gd` is intentional — it detects the floor→air edge for
landing animation logic. Do not remove it.

### State string consistency
States are bare strings. A typo in a `_go("wall_sldie")` call will silently play the fallback
`idle` animation. Consider adding an assertion guard if extending the state machine.

### GDScript 4 syntax
Use `@onready`, `@export`, typed arrays (`Array[Node]`), arrow return types (`-> void`),
and `func` without `var`. Do not write Godot 3-style untyped GDScript.

### Input map actions defined in `project.godot`
Actions: `move_left`, `move_right`, `jump`, `crouch`, `roll` (also used as run).
Do not add or rename actions in code without updating `project.godot`.

### Collision layers
- Physics layer 1: player body, tilemap
- Enemy TriggerArea is on layer 0 / mask 1 (detects layer-1 bodies only)
Keep this convention when adding new `Area2D` or `CharacterBody2D` nodes.

## Sprite Spec (for art replacement)

All player sprites: **48×48 px per frame, single row, no padding**.

| Animation | File | Frames |
|-----------|------|--------|
| idle | character_idle.png | 6 |
| walk | character_walk.png | 8 |
| run | character_run.png | 8 |
| roll | character_roll.png | 11 |
| jump | character_jump.png | 4 |
| air_spin | character_air-spin.png | 8 |
| land | character_land.png | 3 |
| crouch_idle | character_crouch-idle.png | 4 |
| crouch_walk | character_crouch-walk.png | 11 |
| ledge_climb | character_ledge-climb.png | 5 |
| ledge_grab | character_ledge-grab.png | 1 |
| wall_slide | character_wall-slide.png | 2 |
| wall_land | character_wall-land.png | 1 |

Filenames must match **exactly** — the AnimatedSprite2D references them by UID, but the import
system uses the filename as the stable key.
